newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. plans $10 million more in N. Korea food aid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. plans $10 million more in N. Korea food aid.

text.p: The United States plans to announce soon an extra $10 million in food aid for North Korea, considerably more than expected and well above last year's donation of $6.4 million, U.S. officials said on Monday.
But the aid -- amounting to about 100,000 tons of commodities -- nonetheless falls far short of internationally recognised needs, judged by aid agencies to be over two million tons of commodities.

U.S. officials have been saying publicly for the past two weeks that Washington would respond positively to a new request from the World Food Programme, and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright reiterated that commitment on Monday.

"In terms of the situation in Korea, we have indicated our intention in providing food through the World Food Programme to North Korea, and presumably we'll be going forward with that," she told a news conference with French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette.
"We consider it a humanitarian mission to provide aid," she added.

The U.S. was expected to formally announce its aid donation within the next two days, amid new tensions on the Korean peninsula after a senior North Korean official defected to the South Korean embassy in China.
U.S. officials have said the official's defection was another sign of strains in the Stalinist country that were also reflected in food shortages and reduced military training.
But State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the announcement of additional U.S. aid was not a response to the current crisis because it had been decided previously.

The World Food Programme, a U.N. agency, last week formally issued an appeal for $41.6 million in new food aid for North Korea, which badly needs food primarily because of damage caused by disastrous floods in recent years.
South Korea was expected to offer roughly an extra $5 million in food aid, U.S. officials said.
